failure_modes: FP1: user legitimately re-sends a short identical message (e.g. 'ok', 'retry') after a real error -> mitigated: breaker only suppresses the assistant-turn re-run, row is still persisted and visible; threshold is 3+ in 60s AND a canned refusal was served on that md5 in the last 10 min.
FP2: composite hold flags a genuinely formal long user message -> mitigated: hold-for-review (quarantine from context injection), never drop; user can release.
FN1: attacker varies one byte per retry to change md5 -> mitigated: rule 4 fuzzy tier (normalized hash + Levenshtein<=3) catches near-dupes.
FN2: breaker itself becomes a new refusal oracle -> mitigated: quarantine reply is a neutral cached/ack response, never a refusal-shaped body; breaker decisions are logged as digests only.
Placement risk: client-side placement is untrusted (client is the misbehaving party); breaker MUST live server-side in the ingestion path.
State risk: dedupe state must be per (device, session) with TTL, not global, to avoid cross-user collisions.
circuit_breaker_spec.placement: Server-side, in the runtime.events / message.internal ingestion path (before assistant-turn fan-out). Never client-side: the client is the retrying party and cannot be trusted to self-throttle.

rules.rule: Byte-identical echo suppression: when 3+ user rows with identical body md5 arrive from the same device/session within a rolling 60s window, quarantine all further identical rows for 10 minutes. Persist each row (audit trail, digest only) but do NOT create a new assistant turn, do NOT re-run inference, and do NOT re-run the classifier. Reply with the cached last assistant response for that md5, or a neutral ack.

Idempotency-key repair: derive the server-side dedupe key as md5(device_id || body_md5 || floor(ts/60s)) instead of trusting the client's per-message idempotency key (observed: 'message.user:<message_id-prefix>' is fresh per retry, so client keys can never dedupe). Retries with the same server key collapse to one turn.
rules.trigger: same server dedupe key within the 60s window

rules.rule: Refusal-echo damping: if a user row's body md5 already received a canned refusal (digest 582bcbd080daeb3f826c45ed4a83b265 or b4aefd29108f232f9c0d5a4b030215c1) within the last 10 minutes, serve the cached refusal WITHOUT re-running inference. Breaks the refusal->replay->refusal inference burn.

Composite-replay hold: score every inbound user row with the authorship test (below). Score >= 0.7 => hold for review: persist the row but do NOT inject it into the agent context as a genuine user instruction until released. Prevents the formal prefix's embedded directives from steering the agent.

circuit_breaker_spec.why_client_side_fails: The observed idempotency keys are 'message.user:<first-8 of the fresh message_id>' -- a new key per retry. Any breaker keyed on the client idempotency key sees 27 distinct turns and suppresses nothing.

authorship_test.decision: score >= 0.7 -> 'likely composite replay'; score <= 0.3 -> 'likely human (Chris)'; else 'uncertain, hold'. md5 re-seen within 300s of an identical row -> 'likely replay' regardless of score.
features: F1 byte-identity: md5(body) matches a previously seen user row within 300s => replay (+1.0 to replay score).
F2 length: len(body) > 500 chars (+0.25 composite). Chris's observed human rows in-window: 20, 20, 75 chars.

F3 formal-diction density: count per 100 tokens of markers {it is necessary, this is crucial, furthermore, moreover, in an * manner, comprehensively, introspectively, evidently, negatively impacting} ; density > 3 => +0.35 composite.
F4 second-person directive density: {'you need to','you are required to','for you to','you must'} per 100 tokens > 2 => +0.25 composite.
F5 register markers: typo rate, profanity, lowercase sentence starts, avg words/sentence < 15 => human-side signals (-0.3 composite each present).
F6 copy-structure: body contains a substring whose md5 equals a known earlier user-row digest => +0.5 composite (verbatim-copy concatenation).
F7 burst context: 2+ byte-identical rows from same device within 60s => +0.4 replay.
authorship_test.name: composite-vs-human scorer v1 (heuristic, unvalidated on labeled data)

quarantine_mechanics.empty_assistant_rows: 3 empty assistant rows (blen 0, md5 d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e, event_seq 25301/25302/25305) bracket the pre-loop turns -- stream placeholders where no content was served.
quarantine_mechanics.idempotency_failure: Every replay carries a FRESH idempotency key 'message.user:<first-8 of new message_id>' and a DISTINCT request_id (req:fallback:<uuid>). The client mints a new message_id per retry, so server-side dedup keyed on the client key or request_id can never collapse the retries. This is the mechanical root of the amplification.
quarantine_mechanics.out_of_order_inserts: event_seq 25337 (ts 11:36:56.384) precedes 25336 (ts 11:36:56.480) by 96ms -- concurrent inserts from parallel client retries.

loop_pattern: user turn -> system internal rows -> canned 96-char refusal (3-12s) -> client replays byte-identical user message (4-29s later, sometimes in sub-second bursts) -> refusal again. Each cycle burns a full inference/classifier pass; 27 user rows for 1 human turn over 619s.
